newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. ambassador to France condition still serious.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ambassador to France condition still serious.

text.p: U.S. ambassador to France Pamela Harriman remained near death in serious condition in a Paris hospital on Wednesday after suffering a brain haemorrhage, embassy aides said.
Harriman, 76, a close supporter of President Bill Clinton, had fallen ill on Monday evening and was rushed to hospital by ambulance.
"There are no changes in her condition. There are no new developments," one aide said. Others said she was barely clinging to life.
A haemorrhage can severely impair bodily function or lead to death by blocking the blood supply to the brain.
In Washington, the White House said on Tuesday that Clinton and his wife Hillary were concerned about Harriman and were keeping a close watch on her condition.
"They've asked to be kept updated for any information that comes from our embassy in Paris. Obviously, she is in their thoughts and prayers," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
Harriman's son, Winston Spencer Churchill, a British member of parliament and grandchild of the wartime British prime minister, had rushed to Paris upon learning of her illness.
Following reports last year that Harriman wanted to leave Paris, she had issued a statement denying any move was imminent and saying she would follow Clinton's wishes.
Diplomatic sources said she had been expected to retire in June.
